name: killing-assay-cytotoxicity
title: In-vitro-style killing / cytotoxicity assay
question:
In a well-mixed assay, do active T cells produce net tumor cell death (positive
cytotoxicity) relative to a matched no-T control, robustly across seeds?

study_card.goal: Reproduce the paper's in-vitro killing readout: positive cytotoxicity vs. a matched control.
study_card.mechanism: Well-mixed tumor cells (50% PDL1+, MHCI-high) + active T cells (25% PD1+, 1.5:1 ratio). Cytotoxicity = (control - experiment)/control x 100 on final tumor count, paired per seed.
study_card.expected_result: Fewer tumor cells with T cells than in the no-T control (positive mean cytotoxicity).
study_card.main_expert_question: How does cytotoxicity scale with the T:tumor ratio and PDL1+ fraction toward the paper's dose curves?

biological_summary:
Mimicking the paper's cytotoxicity assay, tumor cells were co-cultured with active T cells
at a 1.5:1 ratio against 50% PDL1+ tumors, with a matched no-T control, across 6 seeds. Mean
cytotoxicity was positive (~11% ± 8), positive in 5 of 6 seeds — net killing from cumulative
cytotoxic-packet delivery to MHCI-high tumors. The dense, high-ratio well-mixed layout gives
enough sustained contact for killing to register over the run, unlike the sparser spatial
microenvironment.

expected_behavior.name: positive_cytotoxicity
expected_behavior.en: Mean net tumor reduction vs. the matched no-T control is positive.

measure.of: cytotoxicity = (control_final - experiment_final)/control_final x 100, mean over seeds

report.title: Killing / cytotoxicity assay
report.objective: Show positive, replicated T-cell cytotoxicity vs. a matched control.
report.conclusion:
With a 1.5:1 T:tumor ratio against 50% PDL1+ tumors, active T cells reduce the final tumor
count relative to the no-T control by ~11% on average (positive in 5/6 seeds).
report.caveat:
Single ratio / PDL1+ fraction and reduced scale; a ratio + PDL1+ sweep with more replicates
is needed to reproduce the paper's quantitative cytotoxicity dose curves.

readouts: tumor count over time (+T vs control), mean ± std
